stories.title: Utah State University building earns zero energy certification
stories.summary: The Moab Academic Building has achieved Zero Energy Certification from the International Living Future Institute. Designed by Lake Flato and MHTN Architects, the facility uses building orientation and thermal mass to manage desert temperatures. The design relies on principles used by ancestral Puebloans to stay comfortable without mechanical cooling.

stories.title: Philadelphia duplex draws crowd for passive house tour
stories.summary: A sold-out crowd toured the Passive George duplex in Philadelphia last month to inspect the building envelope before its PHIUS certification. Architect Jeremy Avellino of Bright Common led the event. The project is generating interest within the local passive house community for its approach to carbon-neutral construction.

stories.title: Green Building Congress 2026 to convene in Mumbai
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council will host its 24th Green Building Congress in Mumbai from 26 to 28 November. The event expects over 3,000 delegates and 150 thought leaders to discuss sustainable built environments. The theme for the three-day conference is forging a sustainable future.

stories.summary: Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA has won the inaugural Ambasz-MoMA Annual Prize for Nature-Reconciled Architecture for the Friendship Centre in Bangladesh. The $200,000 award recognizes projects that address the relationship between built and natural environments. Half of the prize money is allocated to a non-profit organization for tree planting.

stories.summary: Consultancy AgRadiance has launched an interactive platform mapping 2,697 agrivoltaic projects across 111 countries. The atlas tracks installations alongside governing rules and incentive schemes. It also records 151 projects that have been deferred or abandoned. The platform plans to integrate a web-based design tool for future users.

stories.summary: The Global Cement and Concrete Association presented a progress report on its 2050 Net Zero Roadmap at COP31. The document details industry efforts regarding alternative fuels, low-carbon concrete and carbon capture technologies. The sector continues to work toward its stated goal of reaching net zero emissions.

stories.summary: The Built99 index has launched to highlight 99 Indian architecture practices based on finished projects rather than portfolios. The project, backed by designboom and ArchDaily, describes itself as an independent cultural institution. It claims to avoid pay-to-play rankings while focusing on responsible construction and long-term cultural value.

stories.title: Delhi and Bihar launch subsidised bus services for Chhath Puja
stories.summary: Ahead of Chhath Puja, the Delhi and Bihar governments have launched 77 inter-state bus services to facilitate travel. Fares are subsidised by up to Rs 1,028. The government says it is committed to ensuring passengers can travel home safely and affordably for the festival period.

stories.title: Mumbai leads Indian cities in registered green building projects
stories.summary: Mumbai has 2,057 projects registered with the Indian Green Building Council, leading all Indian cities. Maharashtra holds 4,754 of the 20,621 total national registrations. Of the city's projects, 920 are commercial and 847 are residential. The number of green projects in Mumbai has increased by 319 since last year.

stories.title: Maharashtra accounts for 30 percent of India's green buildings
stories.summary: Maharashtra represents nearly 30 percent of India's registered green building footprint, with 2.19 billion sq ft of space in the Mumbai region alone. While the state leads the market, commercial projects dominate the sector, raising questions about whether the green movement can expand into the residential housing market.

stories.title: Built99 initiative spotlights Indian architectural practices
stories.summary: Built99 has launched an annual selection of 99 nominated studios, backed by Designboom and ArchDaily. The initiative aims to bridge Indian architecture with the global creative sphere by championing low-impact construction, regional craft, and cultural responsiveness. The project seeks to write a new script for global design.

stories.title: Kengo Kuma completes thatched house in rural Japan
stories.summary: Kengo Kuma and Associates has finished the Kagaku no Sato Main House in Ibaraki Prefecture. The wooden structure features a circular thatched roof designed to appear lifted by the wind. The project recently received the Encouragement Award at the 2026 Wood Design Awards.

stories.summary: Line Arc has designed a 984.91-sqm office space within the Esentai Apartments in Almaty, Kazakhstan. The layout replaces conventional corporate design with hospitality-driven interiors, including a central social café and flexible coworking hubs. The project blends modernism with regional craftsmanship and Kazakh cultural motifs.

stories.title: Think Tank Architecture completes Zando Central Market in Kinshasa
stories.summary: Think Tank Architecture has built a new market in Kinshasa to house 20,000 vendors. The geometric brick-and-concrete structure replaces a historic market demolished due to maintenance issues. The studio used the replacement project as an opportunity to reimagine the role and function of the city's central market space.

stories.title: GT3 Architects details Eclipse Leisure Centre project
stories.summary: GT3 Architects is a finalist for the 2026 Retail and Leisure Architect of the Year Award for its work on the £50 million Eclipse Leisure Centre in Staines-upon-Thames. The facility replaces an ageing centre and was designed to meet specific community requirements for the local borough council.

stories.title: NOA designs prefabricated timber house for relocation
stories.summary: NOA has designed the DeKruif House, a prefabricated residence built from cross-laminated timber. The project is intended for families who do not want to commit to a single location, allowing the home to follow its inhabitants. It was originally envisioned for sites in Canada and Washington.

stories.summary: The University of Queensland is conducting full-scale fire tests on cross-laminated timber ceilings at a Brisbane training ground. stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority has barred promoters from using generic consent forms when altering building plans. stories.summary: The Haryana government has ordered an investigation into Gurugram's drainage issues and set a December 31 deadline for a flood management plan. stories.summary: KW Group acquired a 1.5-acre land parcel in Ghaziabad for 134 crore rupees via auction. The developer plans an ultra-luxury residential project with an estimated gross development value of 877 crore rupees. The acquisition cost excludes stamp duty and registration charges.

stories.summary: India fell five places to 28th in the 2027 Climate Change Performance Index. While the report acknowledges non-fossil energy expansion, it cites continued coal dependence and a lack of a time-bound national energy transition roadmap. India retains an overall medium rating.

stories.title: Inc42 and DevX launch proptech investment pool
stories.summary: Inc42 and DevX have launched RE:FRAME, an investment pool with 15 crore rupees for proptech startups. The initiative aims to address inefficiencies in India's 650 billion dollar real estate market, which remains reliant on traditional, manual processes despite the sector's scale.

stories.title: SketchUp add-on adds BIM for small firms
stories.summary: Archeform BIM has released version 1.1 of its SketchUp extension, focusing on renovation workflows. The tool allows users to model walls, slabs and windows as BIM elements that carry IFC properties. It aims to put permit-ready drawings within reach of smaller practices.

stories.title: V3D Asia enters Malaysian construction market
stories.summary: Japan-based V3D Asia is entering the Malaysian housing market through its subsidiary Nuvah. The company is currently printing five bungalows in Semenyih. It claims that 3D construction printing offers faster build times, lower wall costs and greater design freedom.

stories.summary: Icon is using its Vulcan construction system to print walls for a 12,600-square-foot industrial building in San Antonio. The project includes a steel superstructure for an exhibition area, with completion expected by summer 2027. The 3D-printing tech will only be used on part of the building.

stories.summary: Attentive.ai has completed its first acquisition by purchasing Takeoff Monkey. The company says its Beam AI software currently powers $500 billion in construction bids. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: SecureTech subsidiary signs letter of intent for California project
stories.summary: SecureTech Innovations subsidiary AI UltraProd has signed a non-binding letter of intent to develop a 3D-printed residential project in Concord, California. The proposed Lighthouse project aims to showcase the company's robotic construction technology, starting with a single-story accessory dwelling unit.

stories.title: Torus raises $500 million for prefabricated AI data centers
stories.summary: Utah startup Torus raised $500 million to produce prefabricated AI inference units. The company claims these units require no building construction and can go from contract to running workloads in 12 to 16 weeks. The smallest system is roughly the size of a small cargo van.

stories.title: CEPT University updates BDes Hons admission criteria
stories.summary: CEPT University will accept UCEED and NID DAT 2027 scores for its five-year Bachelor of Design programme. Candidates with valid scores in either national-level examination will be exempted from the university's own entrance test. Applications for the 2027 academic session are open until November 30.

stories.title: IIM Bangalore receives IGBC Platinum certification
stories.summary: IIM Bangalore has become the first educational institution in India to receive Platinum certification under the IGBC Green Campus Rating System. The rating recognises the campus for its sustainability initiatives, including energy efficiency, water conservation, renewable energy use, waste management and overall campus well-being.

stories.title: Raumlaborberlin to lecture at IE University
stories.summary: The Berlin-based architecture collective raumlaborberlin will present a lecture at IE University in Madrid on November 25. The event is part of the 2026-2027 COMMON(S) series and will explore architecture as an experimental, participatory practice that engages communities in the production of urban space.

stories.title: IIM Bangalore earns green campus distinction
stories.summary: IIM Bangalore has received Platinum certification under the Indian Green Building Council Green Campus Rating System. The framework recognises the institution for its efforts in energy efficiency, water conservation and sustainable campus management. It is the first educational institution in India to earn this specific rating.

stories.title: Architecture schools list faculty openings
stories.summary: The Archinect job board currently features 23 architecture schools and universities seeking faculty and academic leadership. Tulane University is among the institutions hiring, with openings for professors of practice and assistant or associate professors in design and architecture. The roundup includes tips for improving portfolios and resumes.

stories.title: University of Virginia names new architecture dean
stories.summary: The University of Virginia School of Architecture has appointed a new dean. The announcement follows a search process for the leadership role. The school remains focused on its academic mission as it prepares for the transition in its administrative office.

stories.title: SPA Bhopal to assist with Odisha infrastructure vision
stories.summary: The State Transport Authority and the School of Planning and Architecture in Bhopal have signed a memorandum of understanding. The partnership aims to support the Viksit Odisha 2036 vision by creating a holistic document for the state's transport infrastructure across air, rail, water and road sectors.

stories.title: Amy Catania Kulper named dean of UVA School of Architecture
stories.summary: Amy Catania Kulper will become the dean of the University of Virginia School of Architecture on January 6, 2027. Kulper most recently served as head of the Bartlett School of Architecture at University College London. She succeeds Malo Hutson, who plans to return to the faculty.

stories.title: UNM architecture student wins On the Brinck prize
stories.summary: Benjamin Mehigan, a Ph.D. candidate at the University of New Mexico, has been awarded the On the Brinck | Places Prize. The award is a partnership between the UNM School of Architecture and Planning and Places Journal, supporting public scholarship focused on the Southwestern United States.

stories.title: Advice for architecture students
stories.summary: New architecture students are entering a field facing high fees, limited contact time and the integration of AI. Despite challenges like the cost-of-living crisis and a competitive job market, the degree remains a wide-ranging educational opportunity. Resilience is suggested for those starting their path.
